_meta.note: Agent-framework how-tos, harness-first (CrewAI + LangGraph exemplars; fan out later). Reproducible pinned Docker per framework so a live proof is re-runnable and dep trees stay isolated (future-proof). HARD constraint: Docker is the on-demand LIVE tier, NEVER a suite gate — run-tests.sh / pytest / parity stay Docker-free and green everywhere. Reproducible environment != reproducible output (the LLM is nondeterministic; a small local model may miss a strict gate by luck), so the containerized proof verifies WIRING (real framework -> real adapter -> real gate produces gate-evaluable output) and is honest that a strict pass depends on model capability. FH0: a DRY parametrized Docker harness (ARG FRAMEWORK/VERSION + pinned matrix + run.sh with a Docker-free --check). LX0: actually build+run the two exemplars against local Ollama, capture RESULTS.md; the deterministic gate asserts conformance + a substantive results record, and the adversarial review validates the live evidence is genuine. GD0: the two guides (division-of-labor for typical framework users, real config, bring-your-own-agent seam, containerized live-proof section) + index/roadmap + a Docker-free T64 suite group. Dominant message: HeartBeat complements the framework (Stage B = reasoner), it does not replace it; the gate is the contract so frameworks are swappable (no lock-in).

tasks.title: Author the harness spec
tasks.description: Spec-first: write tests/frameworks/README.md defining the contract — a parametrized Dockerfile (ARG FRAMEWORK, ARG VERSION) on a shared base, a pinned matrix (framework -> version), and run.sh <framework> [--check]. --check validates WITHOUT Docker (framework is in the matrix with a pin, is a real backend in the registry AND has a pyproject extra, Dockerfile declares the ARGs) and prints FRAMEWORK-HARNESS-OK:<fw>. Live mode builds the pinned image and drives the real adapter against local Ollama (--network host), asserting the wiring produced gate-evaluable output. State the constraint that this tier never gates the suite.

tasks.title: Build the parametrized Dockerfile + matrix + run.sh
tasks.description: Create tests/frameworks/Dockerfile (parametrized: installs heartbeat from the mounted repo + the pinned framework), tests/frameworks/matrix.txt (crewai + langgraph pins to start), and tests/frameworks/run.sh implementing --check (Docker-free validation, derives the registry from py/src/heartbeat/backends and extras from py/pyproject.toml) and the live build+run mode. Verify run.sh --check crewai and --check langgraph both emit FRAMEWORK-HARNESS-OK.

tasks.title: Build + run the two pinned images against Ollama
tasks.description: Run tests/frameworks/run.sh crewai and run.sh langgraph: build each pinned image, drive the real adapter (HB_EXEC_PROVIDER=ollama) against local Ollama through a real HeartBeat project, and record the outcome — framework, pinned version, model, date, and verdict (phase completed / produced output but strict gate is model-luck / model failed) — into tests/frameworks/RESULTS.md with a transcript snippet. Adjust the matrix pin if a build fails, and freeze the working pin.

tasks.title: Write the CrewAI + LangGraph guides
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/use-heartbeat-with-crewai.md and docs/howto/use-heartbeat-with-langgraph.md for typical framework users: lead with the division of labor (defuse the framework-specific confusion — CrewAI 'does your DAG compete with my crew?'; LangGraph 'isn't this a redundant stateful graph?'), the real provider/model config (HB_EXEC_PROVIDER/MODEL, OLLAMA_HOST), the bring-your-own-agent seam (the adapter is a small replaceable file; a custom adapter conforms via build-and-test-a-backend), one gotcha, and a containerized live-proof section pointing at tests/frameworks/run.sh + RESULTS.md. Reference only real commands/backends; do not overclaim drop-in-your-crew.

tasks.title: Index + roadmap + T64 suite group
tasks.description: Add both guides to docs/howto/README.md and flip their rows in docs/howto/howto-list.md; add a T64 group to tests/run-tests.sh that is Docker-free — run.sh --check crewai/langgraph (harness well-formed), crewai+langgraph conformance/degrade, and prose-integrity on the two guides — so the suite enforces the harness + docs without depending on Docker.

GATE_FH0.desc: A DRY, Docker-free-validatable framework harness: --check derives the registry+extras from source and validates the two exemplars; the matrix is well-formed.

review.prompt: Refute that FH0 is done: is --check genuinely Docker-free (no docker invocation)? Does it DERIVE the valid framework set from the registry (backends/__init__.py) and pyproject extras, so a bogus framework or a matrix entry with no extra is rejected (not a hardcoded allowlist)? Is the Dockerfile actually parametrized (ARG FRAMEWORK/VERSION) and does the matrix carry real pins? Could --check pass for a framework that isn't real?

criteria.cmd: bash "$PROJECT_DIR/tests/frameworks/run.sh" --check crewai 2>&1 | grep -q 'FRAMEWORK-HARNESS-OK:crewai' && bash "$PROJECT_DIR/tests/frameworks/run.sh" --check langgraph 2>&1 | grep -q 'FRAMEWORK-HARNESS-OK:langgraph'

criteria.desc: every matrix framework is a real backend with a pyproject extra, and a bogus one is rejected
criteria.cmd: bash "$PROJECT_DIR/tests/frameworks/run.sh" --check not-a-framework 2>&1 | grep -q 'not a real backend' && bash "$PROJECT_DIR/tests/frameworks/run.sh" --check-all 2>&1 | grep -q 'HARNESS-ALL-OK'

GATE_LX0.desc: The two exemplars conform deterministically, and RESULTS.md records a substantive live run for each (evidence validated by review).

review.prompt: Refute that LX0 is done: is the RESULTS.md evidence GENUINE — did the pinned Docker images actually build and drive the real framework against Ollama (re-run tests/frameworks/run.sh langgraph to check), or is it fabricated? Does each entry carry a real pinned version + model + date + an honest verdict (not overclaiming a strict pass if it was model-luck)? Does the deterministic conformance for crewai/langgraph genuinely hold? Is the Docker tier kept OUT of the suite gate?

criteria.desc: RESULTS.md records a substantive run for each exemplar (framework + version + model + date + verdict)
criteria.cmd: for f in crewai langgraph; do python3 -c "import sys,re; t=open('$PROJECT_DIR/tests/frameworks/RESULTS.md').read(); b=re.search(r'(?ims)^#+\s*'+sys.argv[1]+r'\b.*?(?=^#+\s|\Z)', t); s=b.group(0) if b else ''; sys.exit(0 if (b and re.search(r'\d+\.\d+', s) and re.search(r'20\d\d-\d\d-\d\d', s) and ('model' in s.lower()) and ('verdict' in s.lower() or 'outcome' in s.lower())) else 1)" "$f" || exit 1; done

GATE_GD0.desc: Both guides are accurate, reference their proof, are indexed/roadmapped, and the suite enforces the harness + docs Docker-free.

review.prompt: Refute that GD0 is done: does each guide land the division-of-labor for its framework's typical user (CrewAI 'competes with my crew?', LangGraph 'redundant graph?') accurately, or generically? Is the config real (matches the adapter's HB_EXEC_PROVIDER/MODEL/OLLAMA_HOST)? Does bring-your-own-agent overclaim (it must say the adapter is edited, not zero-code)? Is T64 genuinely Docker-free? Any guide missing from index/roadmap, or a proof it cites that doesn't run?

criteria.desc: each guide references its proof and passes prose-integrity
criteria.cmd: cd "$PROJECT_DIR/docs/howto" && grep -q 'tests/frameworks' use-heartbeat-with-crewai.md && grep -q 'tests/frameworks' use-heartbeat-with-langgraph.md && bash gate-examples/prose-check.sh use-heartbeat-with-crewai.md use-heartbeat-with-langgraph.md 2>&1 | grep -q 'ALL-PROSE-OK'
for f in use-heartbeat-with-crewai use-heartbeat-with-langgraph; do grep -q "$f" "$PROJECT_DIR/docs/howto/README.md" && grep -q "$f" "$PROJECT_DIR/docs/howto/howto-list.md" || exit 1; done

criteria.desc: the node suite enforces the harness + guides Docker-free (T64 group PASSED)
